title: Cock a desoldering pump and fire it on the marked joint
instruction: Cock the blue desoldering pump, rest its nozzle on the solder joint that sits on the red sticker, fire the pump there with its white button, then stand the pump back in its holster.
context: Electrical and electronics repairers (O*NET 49-2094) clear a solder joint with a spring-loaded desoldering pump: the plunger is pushed down until a latch catches it, the nozzle is rested on the molten joint with the pump upright, and the button frees the plunger to suck the solder up. A pump that is not cocked does nothing when the button is pressed, and a shot fired off the joint is wasted and the pump has to be cocked again. The plunger's recoil jolts the pump, so it has to be held down on the joint. Here one arm holds the pump while the other presses the button, which sits 8 cm above the hold.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are centres in centimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, table top at height 0. Holster: four dark grey plastic blocks, 5 x 5 cm overall and 2.2 cm tall, round a 1.2 cm square hole, fixed at (27, -15). Pump (about 110 g, standing in the holster with its nozzle through the hole, plunger out): a blue plastic barrel 2.4 x 2.4 cm and 12 cm tall (60 g) resting on the holster's blocks, with a white plastic nozzle 5 x 5 mm and 2 cm long under it; a black plunger (40 g) whose knob is 3 cm across and 1.2 cm thick, 2.6 cm above the barrel's top at rest, on a steel rod, pushed down by a 240 N/m spring (6 N when pushed down 2.5 cm, where a latch holds it); a white button 1.2 cm wide, 8 mm thick and 1.4 cm tall on the barrel's left (+y) side, 1.5 cm below its top, 4 mm of travel, sprung at 1,500 N/m (6 N at the end), which frees the latch once it is pressed 2.5 mm. Circuit board: a green 10 x 8 cm board, 1.6 mm thick, fixed on the table at (31, 0). Solder joints: three silver cylinders 7 mm across and 2.5 mm tall on the board at (31, -2), (31, 0) and (31, 2), fixed. Sticker: a red 1.6 cm square, 0.4 mm thick, flat on the board under the middle joint, which is the one to clean. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured with a ruler and a side photo at the moment of the shot. Cocked: the plunger pushed down 2.4 cm or more, which latches it. A shot: the button pressed 2.5 mm or more while the pump is cocked, which frees the plunger. A shot is good if the centre of the nozzle's tip is within 2 mm of the top of the middle joint and the pump's axis is within 15 degrees of vertical, and near if the tip is within 6 mm of it. The pump is in the holster if its barrel's centre is within 8 mm of the hole's axis and 4 mm of its resting height and the pump is within 5 degrees of vertical. 1.0 (success, held 1 s): a good shot was fired at any point, and at the end the pump is in the holster and still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) with its plunger still. 0.75: a good shot at any point, but the pump is not in the holster and still at the end. 0.5: no good shot, but at any point a shot was fired near the joint. 0.25: no near shot, but at any point the pump was cocked with its tip within 2 mm of the joint's top and within 15 degrees of vertical. 0 otherwise, including doing nothing, pressing the button of an uncocked pump, or firing only at the other joints, and 0 if the pump falls off the table (barrel centre more than 2 cm below the table top).
reset_notes: Stand the pump in the holster with its plunger fully out and its latch free, the button out, and the board and joints as listed. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the demo is open loop and the joints are 2 cm apart.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The pump is a box barrel with a box nozzle bonded under it, a plunger and a button on sprung prismatic joints, drawn as meshes. The latch is the plunger's joint limits, closed when the plunger reaches the bottom and opened when the button is pressed 2.5 mm. The solder is not simulated: a shot is the plunger's visible stroke and the nozzle is not blocked. The board and joints are fixed. The gripper closes with 50 N per pad. Masses are typical values.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right hand takes the pump to the board's edge but never cocks it or fires it on a joint), demo: 1.0 (success at step 658)
